newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oil World sees higher 4th quarter EU seeds crush.
newsitem.headline: Oil World sees higher 4th quarter EU seeds crush.

text.p: Crushings of oilseeds in the European Union were forecast at 7.75 million tonnes in the Oct-Dec 1996 period, up one percent from a year earlier, the independent newsletter Oil World said.
October crushings had been slow but the pace had quickened, helped by the arrival of new crop U.S. soybeans.

Oil World noted protests from environmental groups against gene-modified soybeans, which account for about two percent of the total U.S. crop, but stressed the U.S. would be the only origin able to export large volumes until March 1997.
EU soybean oil was competitive in third country markets.
Soybean processing in the EU fourth quarter total was put at 3.80 million tonnes, up one percent year-on-year and up by 700,000 tonnes from the third quarter of 1996.
Sunseed crushings in Oct-Dec were pegged at 1.72 million (up 17 percent from last year) and rapeseed at 1.80 million, off 14 percent, with other seeds accounting for 430,000 tonnes.

Oil World said the projected gain in the sunseed crush was due to high imports from Russia and Ukraine while the fall in the rapeseed figure was the result of tight supply, weaker imports and unattractive crushing margins. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
